resolve_windows_names.description: `guard.resolve(root, path)` under an absolute root the runner picks for its host (`/v`, or `C:\v` on Windows), with a resolver for which no path exists. `expect.path` is the joined path below the root, `/`-separated, and `expect.warnings` the calls to the guard's warning handler, in order. On Windows the guard refuses a device name or an alternate data stream and calls no handler; elsewhere it accepts the path and warns. A case whose answer differs by host is written once per platform, and the generator writes the `windows` one by loading the reference as on Windows.

resolve_on_disk.description: The real-disk guard's `resolve(root, path)` against a tree built in a scratch directory from `dirs`, `files` and `links` (link path to target text; a target that starts with `/` is rooted at the scratch directory). `root` is relative to the scratch directory, and so is `expect.path`, `/`-separated. A case with a `..` anywhere pins the POSIX rule, where `link/..` is the parent of the link's target. Windows folds `..` as text before it follows a link, so such a case runs on `unix` only, and on Windows the runners check it against where the filesystem puts the path instead. That covers "a chain of links with long targets spends the call budget" too: its targets hold `..`, so on Windows the chain is cheap.

contains_on_disk.description: The real-disk guard's `contains(outer, inner)` against a tree built in a scratch directory, as in `resolve_on_disk`. `outer` and `inner` are relative to the scratch directory and joined to it as text, so a `..` is not folded first. `expect.contains` is the answer. The runners then create `inner` and check that the filesystem puts it inside `outer` exactly when the answer is true, so a case cannot pin a wrong answer. A case with a `..` runs on `unix` only, and on Windows the runners make only the filesystem check.

real_path.description: The real-disk guard's `realPath(path)` (Rust `real_path`) against a tree built in a scratch directory, as in `resolve_on_disk`. A `path` or `expect.path` that starts with `/` is rooted at the real path of the scratch directory; any other `path` is passed as written. Windows folds `..` as text first, which gives the same answers for these cases, so they run on every host.
